title: fix(plugin-approvals): a payload_display lookup target is titled only for a target record the reader may read
body:
Fixes #23637
Clause-②: no

## What this changes

`plugin-approvals`' `enrichRows` titles each lookup in a request's payload snapshot (`payload_display`). The title was read under the system context and narrowed only by the target's declared API exposure (#22738) and, since PR #23629, by the reader's field-level security on the target object. Nothing asked whether the reader may read the target RECORD.

Now, after the exposure gate:

1. **Object-level admission.** The security service's `canReadObject` is asked once per target object, with the reader's envelope minus the operation-private keys. A refused object (or a throw, or any answer but `true`) is not read as the reader at all, so the security middleware has no denial to log for it. No security service, or one without the optional member, leaves every target to step 2.
2. **Row access.** `resolveReadableParentIds` (`@objectstack/core`, the one caller-scoped "which of these records may this caller read" answer the comment, activity, attachment and mail gates ask) is asked once per admitted target object per read, with the reader's context. Sharing and row-level rules decide, as they do for the data door's `$expand`.
3. **Title.** Only the readable ids are titled, by the existing read and FLS pick (`titlesAsServed`, unchanged). An unreadable target gets no display value and the snapshot's stored id stands, the answer a deleted target already gets.

The SUBJECT is not asked: its `record_title`, label and FLS-redacted snapshot are served exactly as before, whatever the reader's access to the subject record (#7497 ruling C, #10749).

Files:
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`: the narrowing in `enrichRows`, the new private `admittedTargetObjects`, the `attachObjectReadAdmission` attach point and its two exported types (`ObjectReadAdmission`, `ObjectReadAdmissionSource`; not re-exported from `index.ts`), docblocks.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approvals-plugin.ts`: one wiring call handing the service the registered `security` service, resolved lazily on every read like the field-visibility source beside it. Without it the admission would be dead in the composed runtime (route-and-surface rule 2).
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lookup-target-title-row-access.integration.test.ts`: new pins.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/implicit-reference-target-lookup.test.ts`: one existing pin counted exactly one `sys_user` read for an implicit-target `user` lookup. It now asserts the two reads that happen: the reader's row-access ask, then the system title read.
- `.changeset/23637-lookup-target-title-row-access.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch.

**The `canReadObject` pre-filter** is used at the coordinator's offer: the same shape as PR #23663 (not landed) uses in `plugin-audit`'s gate. It is CALLED, through the `security` service plugin-approvals already resolves. Nothing in `plugin-security`, `plugin-audit` or `packages/core` changes, and no log is muted, caught or lowered: a reader's own read of an object they may not read still logs its denial.

## Measurement (function level)

Booted on `main` at `286eb9ef32` with the real `SecurityPlugin` composed in front of a real ObjectQL engine over SQLite, with a routed approver who may read the target object's display field (FLS answers the full field set):

- **Before:** `getRequest` and `listRequests` served the target's title in `payload_display` for two denial classes. (1) The target row was hidden from that reader by a row-level rule on an object they may read. (2) The reader had no object-level read on the target object, so the data door refused it. In both classes the data door did not show the record. **Served.**
- **After, without the admission wired:** both titles were withheld, and a readable row of the same object kept its title. The caller-scoped read of the object with no object-level read added **1 WARN denial line per inbox read** (`getRequest`: 1, `listRequests`: 1, one per refused target object per read).
- **After, with the admission wired** (the production wiring): the served answer was the same and **0 WARN lines** were added.

The measurement rig was a throwaway test file in this package's tree. It imported `plugin-security`'s source by relative path read-only, ran three times, and was deleted. It was never committed.

## Pins (`lookup-target-title-row-access.integration.test.ts`)

A real `ApprovalService` on a real ObjectQL over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3, in-memory). Record readability is the one stand-in for `plugin-security`: one middleware per business object refuses a caller with no object read and scopes one with read to its rows. Pins:

- (a) A reader denied the target row gets no title for it, on `getRequest` and `listRequests`, and the stored id stands. The three classes are a row rule on a readable object, no object read, and a self-lookup to a hidden row. The row shape equals that of a deleted target.
- (a-row) Per record, not per object: in one list, the readable row of an object keeps its title while a hidden row of the same object does not.
- (b) Control: a reader who may read every row gets every title.
- (c) One row-access ask per target object per read, naming every id of that object the read titles, on the single read and on a multi-row list.
- (d) The subject is untouched: a reader who may read no subject row gets the subject's title, label and snapshot exactly as the control does.
- (e) With an admission attached:
  - an object it refuses is not read as the reader, and the answer is unchanged;
  - an admitted object is still narrowed by row;
  - the admission is asked once per target object per read, without the operation-private keys.
- (e-closed) A throwing admission, or one that answers anything but `true`, refuses that object; the throw is said once at `warn`. A service without the member reads as before.
- (f) Composed: the real `ApprovalsServicePlugin.start()` hands its service the registered `security` service's admission.

**Red before.** The first five pins were run on the base's source (`286eb9ef32`) before the fix was written: 3 failed / 2 passed. The failures were (a), (a-row) and (c); (b) and (d) passed, as predicted. Pins (e), (e-closed) and (f) were written later; ablation A below restores the old behaviour and reddens all three.

**Ablations.** Each was run through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode under an `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` restore trap, over the pin file's 8 tests, with the red set predicted before each run:
- A, the old behaviour (every exposed target titled, no ask): 6 failed / 2 passed, = (a), (a-row), (c), (e), (e-closed), (f). As predicted.
- B, admission ignored: 3 failed / 5 passed, = (e), (e-closed), (f). As predicted.
- C, one row-access ask per id instead of per object: 2 failed / 6 passed, = (c), (e). As predicted.
- D, the `approvals-plugin.ts` wiring call deleted: 1 failed / 7 passed, = (f). As predicted.

Every restore was proven by blob equal to HEAD (`0e12be2ed246` for A to C, `ffdaebd5269e` for D) and an empty `git diff HEAD`. There was no dist step: both subjects are imported from `src` by relative path.

## Tests and gates

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 78 files / 1080 tests passed at `9e88df4551`. Since then: a changeset text edit, and two merges of `origin/main` (`1ced0f82bd` and `881eeff315`, both `.claude/**` and `scripts/pm/**` only).
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0. `check:test-typecheck` held at 8 files / 324 errors / 27 signatures. `tsc --listFiles` on `tsconfig.test.json` compiles both edited test files, with 0 errors in them.
- `eslint --no-inline-config` over the 4 changed TS files: exit 0, no findings.
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 67 commands. All 67 were run at `9aed095a6e`, each exit captured before any pipe:
  - 65 answered 0 on the first run.
  - `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` first answered 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET (no workspace dist). After a workspace build (75 tasks, exit 0) both answered 0.
  - Re-derived at `37573fbd67`: the same 67. `--ran`: 67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a derived zero), 0 UNRUN.
  - The ratchet and census families (12) were re-run on `37573fbd67`: all exit 0.
- Not run locally, CI's: the full farm, `pnpm lint`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Log interplay with #23279 (measured).** Without the admission, one inbox read added one `[Security] Access denied` WARN per target object the reader may not read at all. With the admission wired, it added zero. No log is muted, caught or lowered here.
- **Degrade in the console (read from source, not browser-measured).** objectui's inbox summary card (`ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` `payloadSummary`, at objectui `28fb2a0`) gives a reference the server could not resolve no row. So an unreadable target renders as a deleted target already does.
- **Fewer field-visibility asks, same answers.** The target object's FLS answer is now asked only for an object with at least one readable id.
- **Observation, not filed: participant names.** `submitter_name` and `pending_approver_names` are still read under the system context. They are the approval's own participants, part of the inbox entry ruling C gives an approver, and not referenced records.
- **Observation, not filed: a self-lookup to the subject record itself.** A lookup that points at the request's own subject record now follows the reader's row access to that record, while `record_title` is served regardless. This is not a disclosure: it is the same title.
- **Ruling C.** This narrowing reads no new meaning into #7497 ruling C. What the ruling gives an approver (the inbox entry, the FLS-redacted snapshot holding the target's id, the actions) is unchanged. Record access to the referenced record stays with object permissions, sharing and row-level rules, which is what is asked here. Nothing is granted.

## Deviations

- File surface beyond the claim's `approval-service.ts` and its tests: `approvals-plugin.ts`, one wiring call for the coordinator-offered admission (see above).
- Commit trailers carry the repository's model-free pair, and this body ends with the repository's session-URL footer (AGENTS.md).
